item.title: I Just Want One More Christmas
item.description: I might have missed my son’s last Christmas with Santa. I was there, and I watched it happen, but it never occurred to me that it might be his last. item.title: I Thought I’d Be Happy When No One Believed in the Elf Anymore
item.description: My giant hanging basket of petunias had fallen from the tiny hook on the porch for what must have been the 11th time that day. From inside my house, I heard the familiar shouts and bumps of a home containing two teenage boys (mine) and two 8-year-olds (one mine, one his best friend). item.title: She May be In Heaven, but I Still Have Coffee with My Mom
item.description: I do not understand how people can get through life without coffee. For me, it is fuel, it gives me energy, and makes me so very happy! Flavored coffee is the best, with lots of milk and sugar. Black coffee? Please, don’t even go there. My mom always loved her coffee too. She would joke that she drank roughly a pot a day, which did not surprise me at all. Mum also loved coffee mugs. item.title: Mom Was the Magic of Christmas
item.description: As I’ve gotten older, I’ve come to realize my mom was the true magic of Christmas. Throughout my childhood, she was the heart and soul of every holiday season, creating an atmosphere filled with warmth, joy, and enchantment. Every December, she transformed our home from top to bottom into a whimsical holiday wonderland. item.title: The Weight of Always Being “On”
item.description: There’s a kind of exhaustion sleep can’t fix. The kind that builds quietly from being needed all the time. It’s the mental load, the emotional load, the “I just need a minute but there are no minutes left” load. item.title: To All the Non-Festive Moms: I See You
item.description: To all the non-festive moms out there: I see you. It’s hard to find you among a sea of holiday sweaters and jingle bells. item.description: The other night, while my 7-year-old son was brushing his teeth, he spotted a shiny candy wrapper sticking out of the bathroom trash can. His eyes widened.
